newsitem.title: USA: Tradelink ties stock drop to name mix-up.
newsitem.headline: Tradelink ties stock drop to name mix-up.

text.p: TradeLink International Inc said it believes the price of the company's stock has dropped over the last week because investors have confused it with TradeLink International Ltd, an unrelated Bahamian company.
The price of Tradelink International Inc's stock has dropped from about 5-1/4 on January 20 to about 2-1/8 yesterday.
According to its press releases, the Bahamian Tradelink was recently formed in order to acquire Vector Aeromotive Corp.
On January 20, the Bahamian corporation announced it had reached an agreement in principal to acquire another aeromotive-related business in addition to Vector.
None of these companies is related in any way to TradeLink International Inc, and management is considering measures to avoid any further possible confusion, Tradelink International Inc said.

TradeLink International Inc president Richard Herbst said no negative news relating to his company was expected nor was he aware of any other reason for a decline in the price of TradeLink's common stock.

"Although we cannot be certain that this confusion precipitated the price drop, given the timing of the Bahamian company's news, the way it was disseminated by the wire service and the subsequent trading of our stock, we have every reason to believe that the real support for our work has not flagged and that once this mistaken identity is recognized, the deviation in our stock price should be rectified," he said.
TradeLink said it intends to close on its previously announced acquisition of Wireless USA following a definitive agreement, which is expected in the very near future.

Advisors to TradeLink have been in contact with several other resellers of wireless communications and long-distance traffic and the company hopes to enter into substantive negotiations for several acquisitions during the current quarter, TradeLink said.
TradeLink said its goal is to acquire synergistic businesses with an aggregate of at least $25 million in revenue before the end of 1997.
TradeLink said sales of its "FonLink" product line have begun.
In addition, an aggressive marketing campaign for busiess communications solutions for North American businesses seeking services in Mexico will be deployed later this month.
Although only minimal revenue from sales has been generated to date, TradeLink said it expects its interactive voice system in Mexico City will be filled to capacity in the next six months.

TradeLink said it will introduce later this year its interactive voice applications for the U.S. trade show and publishing businesses, which are expected to become the most profitable aspects of TradeLink's operations.
TradeLink said it intends to file a registration statement under the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, which will make it a full reporting company under law.
It not currently required to file annual or quarterly reports under the U.S. securities laws.

The registration statement will be filed as quickly as possible following the completion of the audited financial statements for the company's current fiscal year March 31, 1997. There is no assurance as to if or when the Securities and Exchange Commission would declare such a registration statement effective.
